title: Patch locally normal finite intermediate algebras
statement: Let A be a Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with fraction field K. Suppose there is a nonzero f in A such that every prime localization of A_f is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose also that for every maximal ideal m of A there is a finite A-subalgebra C of K [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], contained in integralClosure A K [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], whose prime localizations at primes contracting to m are integrally closed. Then there is a finite A-subalgebra B of K contained in integralClosure A K for which every prime localization B_q is integrally closed.

proof.text: For each finite intermediate algebra C contained in the integral closure, C is a Noetherian domain with fraction field K. The hypothesis on prime localizations of A_f makes A_f a normal domain by the local criterion.

proof.text: C_f is integral over A_f in K and A_f is integrally closed, so C_f = A_f. In particular it is a normal principal localization of C.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, first paragraph: 'Note that R_f = R'_f since R_f is already normal'

proof.text: By openness of the normal locus, the non-normal locus E_C in Spec C is closed. Because C is integral over A, its image Z_C in Spec A is closed. A prime p avoids Z_C if all C_q over p are normal.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, first paragraph: 'Hence by Lemma 0332 the set of primes p' with R'_{p'} non-normal is closed in Spec(R'). Since Spec(R') -> Spec(R) is closed the image of this set is closed in Spec(R). For such a ring R' denote Z_{R'} this image.'

proof.text: For every maximal m the local-approximation hypothesis supplies a finite intermediate algebra C with m outside Z_C. A prime p is contained in some maximal m, and membership of p in a closed Z_C would imply membership of its specialization m. Thus these open complements cover Spec A. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many C_i whose complements still cover.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, third paragraph: 'As Spec(R) is quasi-compact, the above shows that we can find a finite collection R ⊂ R'_i ⊂ K such that ∩ Z_{R'_i} = ∅'

proof.text: Take B to be the subalgebra generated by these finitely many C_i. Their finite sets of module generators together give finitely many integral algebra generators of B. Thus B is finite over A and stays contained in the integral closure.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0333 (lemma-characterize-N-1), proof of (1)+(2) => N-1, algebra.tex lines 45507-45539, third paragraph: 'Let R' be the subring of K generated by all of these. It is finite over R.'

proof.text: For a prime q of B let p be its contraction to A. Choose C_i with p outside Z_C_i, so its contracted prime q_i has normal localization. Since B is integral over C_i, localization at C_i\q_i is integral over (C_i)_q_i inside the common fraction field K, hence equals (C_i)_q_i. A further localization gives B_q, which is normal. This proves local normality everywhere, without identifying B with the integral closure.
